bullets.title: Fed still hawkish: October hold likely, but December hike priced at ~25bp
bullets.body: Fed Governor Waller and St. Louis Fed's Musalem both signaled further rate increases are needed to reach 2% inflation target. Markets pricing 18% chance of an October hike and ~25bp of hikes through year-end; JPM expects a Fed hike this year followed by a hold through 2027. September CPI and PPI print next week (Wed/Thu) with short-dated implied vol potentially rising into the low 20s on a hot number.

bullets.title: 10-year yield risk range 5.20–5.35%; equity premium at NASDAQ-bubble lows
bullets.body: 10-year yield at 5.3% with real rates near 2.9%; 62% of surveyed investors expect 5.25–5.50% over the next 6 months. The equity premium (earnings yield minus real 10yr) sits at its lowest since the late-1990s NASDAQ bubble, while consensus 5-year earnings growth forecasts are at record highs — implying corporate margins would need to reach 27% within five years from already-record levels.

bullets.title: S&P 500 +0.4% / Nasdaq +0.8% pre-market; 68% of SPX stocks advanced in quad2 correction
bullets.body: Hedgeye's McCullough notes 8 of 11 sectors and ~68% of stocks advanced on the session; SPX immediate-term risk range 7,652–7,850. VIX at 14.91 (-3.2%). Broad tape higher with Bitcoin at ~$81k (trend support ~$75k) and crypto/risk-on names (RDDT, HOOD) leading on the upside.

bullets.title: SpaceX $8B 800MHz spectrum buy: tower stocks +7–12%, telecoms -10–12%
bullets.body: SpaceX acquired ~13.5–14 MHz of 800MHz low-band spectrum from Grain Management for ~$8B (~$1.70/MHz-PoP), moving closer to becoming a wireless carrier and threatening T/TMUS/VZ by 2030. Citi's Mike Rollins sizes 21% upside for CCI, 20% for SBAC, 10% for AMT; upgrades tower ranking order to CCI > SBAC > AMT. T fell 9.9%, TMUS 12.1%, VZ 10.3% on competitive risk; VZ's large C-band holdings could see the largest implied value uplift from higher spectrum prices broadly.

bullets.title: Apple cuts iPhone 18 Pro builds 15–20% on weak demand after $100+ price hike
bullets.body: Nikkei reported Apple instructed suppliers to cut iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max component orders by at least 15% in October; AAPL down ~2.3% pre-market. The iPhone Duo launching Oct 23 at $1,999 also expected to see weak demand. SWKS (~60% AAPL revenue) and QRVO (~50%) are at direct risk from the cuts.

bullets.title: PC shipments collapsed 20% y/y in 3Q26; inventory glut persists
bullets.body: IDC reported 3Q26 global PC shipments fell 20.1% y/y to 62.7M units — far worse than 2Q's 3.8% decline — driven by pull-forward exhaustion ahead of memory price increases. HP Inc fell 30.9% y/y, Dell 25.0%, Apple 11.3%. KeyBanc's Sept notebook ODM check (13.8M units, -18% y/y vs 15.3M estimate) corroborates, with AMD, INTC, MU, and NVDA all negatively impacted by PC exposure.

bullets.title: LITE sold out through early 2029; optical component shortage deepens AI infrastructure constraint
bullets.body: Lumentum CEO confirmed optical components for AI servers are completely sold out through early 2029 — six months longer than prior guidance — with 70% of 2027 demand unmet for some products. LITE up ~6–7% pre-market; sympathy moves in AAOI, COHR, TSEM, GLW, CIEN, FN. This supply constraint is a binding limit on AI data center buildout timelines.

bullets.title: AI capex financing wave: SpaceX $40B, Oracle GPU deals, Broadcom $50B+ for OpenAI
bullets.body: SpaceX is seeking ~$40B in financing for NVIDIA chips (~$30B IG debt, ~$10B bank loans); Oracle is in discussions with Apollo and Goldman for GPU purchase financing; Broadcom is arranging $50B+ in financing for custom chips for OpenAI with Apollo and Blackstone as potential lenders. NVIDIA announced a $500B third-party capital pool dedicated to AI compute financing — GPU-backed debt is becoming a structural component of the AI funding ecosystem, and AI infrastructure borrowing is pushing credit default premiums on major tech issuers to record highs.

bullets.title: OpenAI ARR clarified: $50B net in Sept, targeting $70B+ exit 2026 — gross vs. net confusion
bullets.body: OpenAI's widely-cited $50B September ARR figure is net revenue; the company projects $70B+ net ARR by end of 2026, not a miss. Gross vs. net confusion is driving market volatility. The broader AI lab ecosystem needs $400–600B combined ARR exiting 2027 to support 2029–30 capex plans; 54% of investors don't expect compute oversupply until 2031+.

bullets.title: Agentic AI (Meta Muse/Instinct, Google) poses structural threat to OTA commission pools
bullets.body: Meta's Muse and Instinct now complete full travel bookings — including payment — without OTA or hotel integration, bypassing intermediaries entirely. OTA stocks (BKNG, ABNB, EXPE) are down 15–25% following agentic tool launches. None of the 11 tracked OTAs/hotel brands have built systems allowing outside agents to complete bookings independently; Expedia leads readiness, Hyatt and Airbnb lag. Hotels are positioned to benefit while OTA commission income faces deflationary pressure.

bullets.title: Data center supply/demand imbalance widening through 2028; labor the binding constraint
bullets.body: Jefferies forecasts 12.9 GW new North American data center capacity in 2026, 18 GW in 2027, and 26 GW in 2028, with ~33% growth this year sustained through 2028. ~65 GW is under construction (~140% of installed capacity) but labor shortages are the primary bottleneck — US electrician employment grew only 15% 2020–2025 while 2027 capacity deliveries are expected to be 6x higher. DLR/EQIX own ~3 GW in the most supply-constrained markets; former BTC miners (HUT, WULF) transitioning to AI data centers offer significant revenue upside.

bullets.title: Brent at $99 ($96–$106 range); oil/refiners/shipping longs intact heading into CPI
bullets.body: Hedgeye's McCullough is maintaining long positions in Brent crude, shipping, and refiners but selling strength at the upper end of risk ranges. WTI broke its trade level (~$91/$87); Brent shows better trend signal. MPC 3Q EPS estimated at $26.56 vs. consensus $24.28 on blended crack spreads +45% q/q. Copper up 2% on Chile Antofagasta strike (35% of annual production at risk); copper remains bullish on trade and trend.

bullets.title: Taiwan exports +61% y/y in September; TSMC revenue at fresh USD records — sustained AI demand signal
bullets.body: Taiwan September exports surged 8% m/m and 61% y/y, doubling over three years on AI chip demand. ICT products hit an all-time high of $41B, up 8x since 2023. TSMC monthly revenues reached nearly NT$500B with fresh USD records. Taiwan Manufacturing PMI jumped to 56.7% — a reading with 70% correlation to US ISM, leading by one month.

bullets.title: Goldman overweight US equities vs. EM/China as 33-year wealth-creation call; concentration at record
bullets.body: Goldman's Mossavar-Rahmani reaffirms overweight US / underweight EM/China as the most wealth-creating allocation call over 33 years. However, only 46% of S&P 500 stocks trade above their 200-day average, and the top 5 stocks equal the bottom 434 — the highest concentration on record. Classic 60/40 is impaired by positive stock-bond correlation; Timmer recommends diversifying into TIPS, leveraged loans, gold, Bitcoin, and commodities.

bullets.title: BoE and Riksbank both likely to hike in November; Norges Bank in 1Q27
bullets.body: JPMorgan shifted its Riksbank call to November (from December), citing board members Thedéen and Seim strongly favoring a hike; Swedish core CPIF surprised to the downside at 0.5% YoY but JPM revises forecasts higher through 2027. BoE MPC commentary also aligns with a November hike given sticky ~3.5% wage settlements; UK 3Q GDP tracking ~2% annualized. Norwegian core CPI-ATE at 3.0% YoY with Norges Bank at 4.5%; JPM expects a further hike in 1Q27.

bullets.title: EU-China trade: managed agreement talks progressing; escalation postponed past Oct 15 summit
bullets.body: EU trade commissioner in Beijing pursuing a 'managed trade agreement' on Chinese hybrid vehicle exports amid a €100B/quarter bilateral deficit. A joint statement on hybrid vehicle tariff rate quotas and rare earth 'green channels' signals modest progress; consultations will continue beyond the Oct 15 EU leaders summit, postponing immediate escalation. Germany's Federation of German Industry has shifted to support trade confrontation after years of resistance.

bullets.title: Brazil election: right leads into runoff; BofA overweight on easing cycle and re-rating potential
bullets.body: Flávio Bolsonaro enters the runoff with a ~6%+ lead; PL's strong congressional performance could support fiscal adjustment via constitutional measures. BofA remains overweight Brazil, drawing parallels to 2018 when local investors poured ~R$200B into equity funds and the Ibov reached 14x forward P/E vs. 9.4x currently. Beneficiaries include capital markets, bond proxies, and leverage plays.

bullets.title: NFLX preparing ~5% workforce RIF; announcement expected before earnings
bullets.body: Netflix is preparing to lay off approximately 5% of its workforce as part of a restructuring, per Puck News, with an announcement expected before earnings. No operational or guidance change attributed to the cuts in current commentary.

bullets.title: China Golden Week: traffic resilient, per-capita spending down 1.9% — cautious consumer
bullets.body: China's 2026 Golden Week saw travel passenger growth of +6.3% y/y but tourism revenue only +4.3%, implying per-capita spending fell 1.9%. Outbound travel surged +9.3%, diluting domestic consumption. PBOC signaled it wants to discourage CNY appreciation bets; Beijing sees no benefit from a stronger yuan while the economy struggles.

bullets.title: US household debt-to-income at 91% (lowest since 1997); saving rate decline driven by liability surge, not asset sales
bullets.body: JPMorgan finds the 2pp decline in the US personal saving rate from 4Q23 to 2Q26 owes entirely to a 1.9pp jump in liability accumulation as a % of disposable personal income — 'other' liabilities (private loans, trade payables) surged 2pp of DPI. Fixed income asset accumulation collapsed 6.4pp of DPI as households bet on equities. Debt-to-income at 91% is historically healthy; 2023 crisis dynamics are not repeating.
